articles.title: Nintendo Pays Homage to Original 1998 Commercial for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in New Remake Trailer
articles.summary: Nintendo has released a new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake trailer that pays homage to the 1998 commercial for the N64 masterpiece — and we’ve got a comparison video showing just how close it is to the original.
articles.body:
Nintendo has released a new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake trailer that pays homage to the 1998 commercial for the N64 masterpiece — and we’ve got a comparison video showing just how close it is to the original.

Cast your mind back to 1998 and you might remember seeing a commercial for Ocarina of Time that had phrases like “A dark time is approaching,” “Willst thou run?” and “Have ye what it takes?” It’s an iconic advert that certainly got my teenage blood pumping at the time.

Now, Nintendo has recreated the advert in a new trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake. It features some of the same shots and even some of the same language. “Willst thou flee? Or Fight?” the trailer asks, leaning heavily on nostalgia as Link encounters Ganondorf on his horse — just as we see him do in the original trailer.

Check out a comparison in the video below.

Reaction to the new trailer has been overwhelmingly positive, with warm memories of weekends spent in the glow of a CRT television successfully rekindled. “THEY DID THE TRAILER THING OMG,” one person said. “NO WAY THEY DID IT,” another added. “THY WILL PREORDER AS SOON AS THY GETS PAYDAY,” one fan joked.

There is one major difference though: Nintendo’s recreation does not include the custom-recorded version of the track "Riddle of Steel / Riders of Doom" from the 1982 film Conan the Barbarian, as the original trailer did. Music rights!

Marketing for the Ocarina of Time remake has ramped up, with Nintendo releasing a number of new commercials ahead of the game’s November launch. Nintendo recently released two new TV spots for Japan that, while brief, reveal a tantalizing glimpse at some never-before-seen characters, chief among them Dark Link .

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots

As Nintendo has pulled back the curtain on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , we’ve begun to get a better understanding of how this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will look and feel to play. IGN has already got you covered with an extensive hands-on preview , as well as a roundup of all the changes we’ve noticed so far compared to the N64 masterpiece.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. While you wait, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview.

articles.title: Potential Steam Deck 2 Chip Shows Up in Leaked Benchmarks, Yet Another Potential Final Fantasy-Themed Codename
articles.summary: We've known for a while that Valve is working on a Steam Deck 2, but it's waiting for a chip that'll provide a "true next-generation" experience. Now, though, a potential APU for the handheld has appeared online, sparking speculation that work is ramping up.
articles.body:
We've known for a while that Valve is working on a Steam Deck 2, but it's waiting for a chip that'll provide a "true next-generation" experience . Now, though, a potential APU for the handheld has appeared online, sparking speculation that work is ramping up.

The benchmark was posted on OpenBenchmarking , and shows an AMD APU codenamed 'Gainsborough,' with 6 cores and 12 threads, along with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory. However, while the the CPU side of the leaked chip is much more powerful, with 50% more cores, there is no information about the GPU, with even the graphics architecture remaining a mystery.

It's not the first time that the Gainsborough chip has appeared online. Earlier this month, Moore's Law is Dead spotted import documents for the chip, using the same 'GBR' abbreviation as the leaked AMD engineering sample. It is possible that this won't be the chip used in the final version of the Steam Deck 2, but the original Steam Deck APU was codenamed 'Aerith,' then the Steam Deck OLED got the 'Sephiroth' chip, so there's clearly a theme going with AMD's codenames for handheld chips.

Steam Deck OLED: White Edition - Slideshow Gallery

At first glance, the performance on the leaked Gainsborough chip doesn't look super impressive, clocking in with a FurMark score of 3,508 points, compared to 3,323 points on the original Steam Deck, according to TechPowerUp . However, the new chip was tested at a lower 768p resolution than the Steam Deck's 800p, which likely makes up for some of the difference. Plus, this is an engineering sample likely running on very early drivers, so there's a lot of room for improvement before this chip ever sees the light of day — if it even does.

These benchmarks don't really say much about how the Steam Deck 2 will actually perform when it actually comes out, either, but their existence suggests Valve's next handheld is closer than I thought. But, if we're at the point where Valve is just trying to nail down the drivers before it makes an announcement, I could see the handheld launching in the next year or two.

Whenever the Steam Deck 2 comes out, it'll launch into a gaming hardware market that's vastly different than when the Steam Deck first came out in 2022. Valve has said that the ongoing RAM crisis hasn't changed its plans for the sequel , so I wouldn't be surprised if it ends up being much more expensive than the original handheld.

Valve has also had to learn the new hardware landscape the hard way, launching the Steam Machine and Steam Frame at prices a lot of gamers have balked at . Valve has even had to raise the price of the Steam Deck so much that it makes it hard to recommend in the face of newer, more powerful handheld gaming PCs .

articles.title: ‘If Hits Are Unexpected, Datasets Aren’t Gonna Get You There’ — Take-Two Interactive and Sony Bosses Say That AI Cannot Replace Human Creativity
articles.summary: Strauss Zelnick and Hiroki Totoki said that AI would not replace human creativity in the entertainment business, but they both still see it as a tool useful to the production pipeline.
articles.body:
Strauss Zelnick and Hiroki Totoki, the heads of Take-Two Interactive and Sony Group Corporation, agreed that AI won’t replace humans in the entertainment business during a talk at the Paley International Summit in New York City on Tuesday morning. They did, however, explain that they do see the technology as a valuable tool.

“I don’t think an AI could replace humans because, particularly in the entertainment field, I think creativity is quite important. Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said. “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”

“One of our division heads has said to his team, ‘You’re not gonna be replaced by AI, but if you’re not careful you’ll be replaced by someone who knows how to use AI,’” Zelnick said. “I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward looking. [...]"

“When the first Grand Theft Auto was created, we thought the phrase ‘Grand Theft Auto’ wouldn't turn into what it’s turned into today,” Zelnick continued, then launching into an anecdote of his stint as president and chief operating officer of 20th Century Fox (now called 20th Century Studios).

“One of the biggest movies I was responsible for, Home Alone — it was completely unexpected. It went into production at Warner Bros. and they put it into turnaround four days into production, which [...] never happens. [...] Everyone thought it was a disaster. And It turned out to be the highest grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are.”

AI use in the production pipeline for games, movies, and TV is a hot-button issue. Just this week, a business strategist at Xbox posted (and then deleted) the "truth that nobody wants you to know" about how "gaming is the only industry pretending not to use AI," and Steam users implored the company to ban AI slop from the next Steam Next Fest. Last week, Epic Games revealed that its new store launcher was vibe coded . But Biddy Blas? AI could never.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

articles.title: Bethesda Reveals What's Coming Next to Fallout 4 With First-Look at a Trio of New Mods
articles.summary: Bethesda has put its weight behind a trio of new Fallout 4 mods as part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations.
articles.body:
Bethesda has put its weight behind a trio of new Fallout 4 mods as part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations.

The Verified Creations label sees Bethesda support modders in an official capacity as they build upon the now 11-year-old post-apocalyptic role-playing game. First up we have FEVer Dreams, from Kinggath Creations, which comes out today, October 20. It’s a free escape room-style dungeon that “inundates players with hallucinations and flashbacks, including conversations with their spouse.” What’s interesting here is FEVer Dreams features the voice of Courtenay Taylor, who played the female sole Survivor in Fallout 4, and Brian T. Delaney, who played the male Sole Survivor in Fallout 4. That’s pretty impressive for a mod!

Meanwhile, Command Override, from Hobgoblin Studios, lets players see through a robot’s eyes and pilot it remotely. It includes a new robot hacking ability, a Robco headquarters dungeon, and — in a first for Verified Creators — a live action trailer. Command Override launches for Fallout 4 on October 21.

And finally, Fathomless, from Zone Zero Creations, is described as a cosmic horror expansion set deep within the Atlantic Ocean. “Following the path of an ambitious pre-war expedition, the sole survivor descends to a mysterious deep-sea crater,” the official blurb reads. It features a new underwater worldspace and interiors, a new storyline with voiced dialogue, and over five unique enemy NPCs. This one’s out in 2027.

These new mods come out during Bethesda’s official Fallout Day celebrations. Fallout Day itself is this Friday, October 23 (October 23, 2077 is of course the day in the Fallout timeline the bombs fell, sparking The Great War that caused the irradiated wasteland fans of the franchise have been playing in over the last few decades).

Fallout’s 30th anniversary arrives next year, so expect some big announcements from Bethesda then. What’s it working on? It’s got everything from Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters to Fallout 5, with an Obsidian-developed Fallout spinoff in there somewhere. Work continues on Fallout 76 and Fallout Shelter, and Season 3 of the Fallout TV series is also incoming. In short, Microsoft is doubling down on Fallout, with new Xbox boss Asha Sharma striving for increased profitability.

articles.title: Cyberpunk TCG Reveals Edgerunners: Burn Bright Set for Spring 2027
articles.summary: Get an exclusive first look at Cyberpunk TCG: Edgerunners: Burn Bright, featuring cards for Maine and Falco, an all-new rarity tier, and a Spring 2027 launch.
articles.body:
After an immensely successful Kickstarter campaign , the first set of the Cyberpunk Trading Card game is now rolling out to stores and backers. But, like any other TCG out there, once one set releases, thoughts and eyes start looking towards what’s next and coinciding with the release of Netflix’s Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 today, the folks at WeirdCo are starting to peel back the digital curtain on what (and when) you and your crew can expect from the second set. Along with some sweet art reveals, exclusively here on IGN.

Launching in Spring 2027, Cyberpunk TCG – Edgerunners: Burn Bright, looks to feature and bring Netflix’s Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime into the world of trading card games. Specifics around the set itself, such as what products it will include or how many new cards it will add to the mix remains a mystery, with the team planning a host of card reveals and details in the coming months. That said, we do have some confirmations, and samples, of some of the artwork players will see on their new cards, including the likes of Maine and Falco from David’s crew in the anime!

Starting with Maine, the head of the crew that Edgerunner’s protagonist, David, would eventually join with, his artwork features his signature red shades, with the appropriate title of “Badass Shades”. Nothing about the specifics of the card have been shared just yet, but just by the name, I think it’s a safe guess that this will be a Gear card, a type of card that you can equip to a Unit or Legend to give them a sort of boost.

Sticking with someone with ties to Maine’s and David’s crews, the next piece of artwork we get to reveal for you chooms is “Falco Hang on Tight!”, complete with the getaway driver’s signature mustache. Again, no real information on what the card is or what it does, but put my eddies down on Legend.

The new, more anime-inspired artwork on these cards look striking and I’m eager to see more. With the new series launching, it will be curious to see just what the split will end up being between Edgerunners and Edgerunners 2 representation in the final set, and all the cards. Speaking of the cards, one additional bit of info WeirdCo has shared is that Burn Bright will feature an “all-new chase rarity” that will be revealed at a later date, adding to Cyberpunk TCG’s collector-friendly nature.

The full retail launch of the launch set, “Welcome to Night City” is set for November 6, 2026 with prerelease events scheduled for the weekend before.

articles.title: AMD is bringing FSR 4.1 to Xbox consoles and handhelds
articles.summary: AMD’s latest upscaling tech is also coming to laptops and 6000-series GPUs.
articles.body: AMD has just revealed that it’s bringing its latest upscaling technology, FSR 4.1, to the Xbox Series S and X consoles, as well as laptops, 6000-series GPUs, and handhelds like the Xbox Ally X devices. FSR 4.1 will start appearing for Radeon RX 6000-series GPUs today, as well as Ryzen AI Max 300 and 400 series devices, and Ryzen AI 9 300 and 400 series devices. AMD launched its FSR 4.1 update for Radeon RX 9000-series graphics cards in March, and promised to bring the technology to older GPUs and handhelds this year. FSR 4.1 can improve performance in more than 300 supported games, including Cyberpunk 2077, Battlefield 6, and Assassin’s Creed Shadows. FSR 4.1 arrives just weeks after Sony and AMD teamed up to bring Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) to the base PS5, based on Sony and AMD’s Project Amethyst work. “We want to bring that work to more gamers,” says Jack Huynh, senior vice president and general manager of AMD’s computer and graphics group. “We didn’t just bring it over, we made it better. We went back into the model, we tuned it and optimized the code path.” While owners of Radeon RX 6000-series GPUs and Gorgon Halo- or Strix Halo-powered devices will get FSR 4.1 today with the latest Adrenalin Edition 26.10.1 drivers, Xbox console owners will have to wait a little longer. “We’ve worked very closely with AMD to optimize this technology, giving developers another powerful tool for great performance and visual quality for players,” says Xbox CTO Scott Van Vilet. “Our teams are continuing to work together across hardware and software, and there’s even more ahead with Project Helix, leveraging FSR Diamond to power what comes next.” FSR 4.1 could have a big impact on Xbox console games, particularly on the lesser powered Xbox Series S. Neither Microsoft or AMD will say when FSR 4.1 will arrive on Xbox consoles, with it simply listed as “coming soon.”

articles.title: Wicker Is an Immersive and Romantic Journey Starring Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, and Peter Dinklage
articles.summary: Wicker review: An immersive and romantic journey to a dark and whimsical reality just beyond our own.
articles.body:
As we’ve learned from stories like Edward Scissorhands, Pinocchio, and Lars and the Real Girl, few things teach us more about what it means to be fully human and alive than creatures crafted by an artist's hands and the desires of one desperate for connection.

A lonely Fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) rebels against the limits, forced and chosen, of her lot in life and entreats a Basket Weaver with mystical skills (Peter Dinklage) to craft her a husband made of wicker (Alexander Skarsgård). Despite its unusual premise, Wicker is surprisingly straightforward in its sweetness and condemnation of small cruelties. There are darker elements to the fantasy, including implied violence, visible gore, and the stark reality that frequent death was a fact of this time period, but these ultimately highlight moments of beauty and affirm the need to savor life’s pleasures, be they exultant or sensual. On the whole, the film is warm and charming with real pathos, largely due to the exemplary cast led by Colman, who seemingly effortlessly elevates both the bawdy comedic beats and moments of sorrow and joy. In lesser hands, the humor might have read as pedestrian, and the relationships distant and unrelatable.

Based on the short story The Wicker Husband by Ursula Wills-Jones and directed by Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson (Save Yourselves!), Wicker is set in a generic medieval village where all the townspeople are known only by their trade (if male) or their husband’s vocation (if female). The one exception is the Fisherwoman, who has either rejected, or been rejected by, the traditional confines of marriage and as such is known by her profession. The townspeople limit her participation in their world to the periphery, ostensibly due to her potent scent (an occupational hazard). But it’s the Fisherwoman’s refusal to fit into the tightly bound structures their culture demands — which the seaside village’s matriarch, the Tailor’s Wife (Elizabeth Debicki), enforces with an imperious smile — that truly drives her to the edges of their community.

These social constraints feel claustrophobic for everyone, most notably the Fisherwoman, who responds with rebellion, and the Tailor’s Wife, who tries to control others as much as she herself feels confined. That suffocating undercurrent is reinforced by the visual storytelling: The town reads as small and hastily constructed, and the interiors are often dim and candlelit even in daylight, shrouded in mystery (in the Basket Weaver’s workshop) or stifled by the darkness of ignorance (in the villagers’ homes). For the length of the film, we too feel trapped in this deeply flammable village (everything seems to be made of hay or wood!). By contrast, the Fisherwoman’s cottage, set apart from the village, is isolated but surrounded by space, fresh greenery, and a sense of liberation. When the Wicker Husband gets his hands on it, the cottage evolves into something artistically shaped and deeply cared for, a reflection of how he sees his wife; it’s as if the Basket Weaver has passed his artistry on to his creation.

The Wicker Husband himself is stunning, as are all of the Basket Weaver’s designs (even the most ghastly of them), particularly set against the grimier village, where most things and often people are covered in dirt or filth. Weta Workshop built the Wicker Husband with CGI enhancements to appear delicate and precious. When he is damaged, the audience understands that the harm illustrates our own failure to care for something of value. Though eerie, he has the essence of Skarsgård’s natural beauty, and is at once a thing other than human and something more. The actor’s placid tones reflect the character’s innocence, perfectly capturing the Wicker Husband’s ability to point out what isn’t working in the human world simply through his ignorance of it or non-participation in it.

Initially, the Fisherwoman’s purchase of her husband and companion is an act of defiance. She is taunting the villagers, turning their tendency to strip away humanity and objectify themselves and one another on its head. In a reversal of roles, she keeps her title as Fisherwoman while her mate is known simply as the Wicker Husband. This is particularly repellent to the Tailor’s Wife, largely because she longs for the freedom and purpose the Fisherwoman enjoys. In reality, work is both a necessity and a gift for the Fisherwoman, who lacks the privileges of those more embedded in society’s conventions. It gives her meaning but leaves her mostly friendless and often filthy. This exiled, misunderstood woman finds, in the prickly arms of a man made of wood, the acceptance and care missing from much of her village life. The Fisherwoman develops deeper affections for her Wicker Husband than she anticipated and in doing so falls prey to the frailties of real attachment, including jealousy and mistrust, even toward a husband she theoretically “owns” (and who could double as furniture).

The actors ground us in this heightened fable. Early in the film, in a glance of no more than 30 seconds, Colman and Debicki convey the entire shared history of two women who understand, envy, and loathe one another. More saliently, it’s here, with one double take from Colman, that we understand Debicki’s casual mean-spiritedness has sealed the town’s fate: The Fisherwoman will have her say, and with it, a husband the likes of which they cannot imagine — one who will challenge their way of life. Colman brings us into the Fisherwoman’s exuberance as she discovers the nightly joys the Wicker Husband offers, without making it so comical that we’re held at a distance from the character. She delivers a performance that gives the audience catharsis as she moves from deep vulnerability and self-sabotage to a woman who takes the gift she’s given and runs with it.

In a sense, the film asks the viewer to examine how much good we allow ourselves before we damage it, often out of fear that it isn’t real or earned and will therefore betray us. The Fisherwoman, who’s been told she’s not worth much, must wrestle with granting herself permission to feel pleasure (often in spades) and with believing that the sweet can, at the very least, equal the bitter in life. Through witnessing her unorthodox relationship, the whole village is faced with the same inquiry. This is the film’s most interesting idea.

Thematically, Wicker hits at patriarchy with the subtlety of a cudgel. Even in name, the women are reduced to property. The Tailor’s Wife is petty, passive-aggressive, and destructive, in no small part because her natural genius is underused at best and entirely suppressed at worst. We see villagers’ lives imperiled because no one has the will to say that those in charge of critical infrastructure are drunk, incapable, or (often) both. Everyone pays a price for these encrusted traditions. The film is an overt morality play, but with enough surreal humor to keep it from feeling laborious or patronizing.

To its credit, Wicker is seeded with more than just an indictment of utterly ruinous bias. It examines, lightly and with a lot of whimsy, why we all as men and women stay loyal to the restrictions that create pain and discomfort for us, be they social norms or internal limitations. It also asks about the bounds of nature itself, as the Basket Weaver defies the “no” life has given this village's residents. He’ll help them reach for their deepest desires so long as they’re willing to name what they want (whether anyone agrees or not) and care for the small miracles he provides.

Dinklage’s Basket Weaver stands apart from the town but, unlike the Fisherwoman, not in opposition to it. In that sense, he serves as the audience’s surrogate: a somewhat objective observer or Greek chorus who at times goes so far as to monologue or narrate events and who casts the final judgment. Dinklage brings a sense of delight to the role, embodying the Basket Weaver’s love of creating within challenging frameworks, and of doing more than he ever thought himself capable of. He also endows the character with empathy without overplaying his hand. His compassion is reserved chiefly for outsiders like the Fisherwoman, and he disdains the villagers’ inability to extend it to her or even themselves.

It takes a man made of wicker to show this town what it is to be complete and fully human. His way of seeing the world, free of the polluting influence of cultural programming, serves as an (often unwanted) mirror for the villagers, exposing the insanity of mundane life. Ultimately, the film celebrates the rewards of being bold and going for what you want (be that family, vocation, both, or something else altogether) without the need for approval. Though the storytelling in Wicker is fairly direct, Fischer and Wilson have steady hands, and the technical elements combined with the talented cast create an imaginative, immersive, and relatively quick (about an hour and 45 minutes) visit to a universe just to the left of our own, granting us enough distance to see ourselves more clearly.

articles.title: Junior Caminero’s ALCS Game 6 Rays HR was unprecedented in multiple ways
articles.summary: With the Tampa Bay Rays eliminating the Cleveland Guardians from the ALCS after a 7-3 win in Game 6, a big moment in the game was the home run from Junior Ca...
articles.body:
With the Tampa Bay Rays eliminating the Cleveland Guardians from the ALCS after a 7-3 win in Game 6, a big moment in the game was the home run from Junior Caminero in the seventh inning. As the blast by Caminero for the Rays was pivotal in giving the team a comfortable lead, the home run was also unprecedented in multiple ways.

Happening in the seventh inning, Caminero hit the home run off of Guardians closer Cade Smith, tied for first in the MLB with 41 saves to go along with a 1.95 ERA. Boasting a productive splitter, Caminero hit the home run off of it, making it the first time that has happened in Smith's career, to go along with it being Caminero's first playoff home run in his career.

"That blast was an unlikely two-run home run against All-Star closer Cade Smith in the seventh inning of the Rays' pennant-clinching win. Never had Smith allowed a homer on his splitter in his major league career. Then Caminero turned on one in on his hands and clanked it off the foul pole to ignite a raucous celebration of his first career postseason home run," Castillo wrote at ESPN.

How Rays' Junior Caminero and his celebration were historic

Caminero is in the midst of a great season for the Rays, recording a .276 batting average to go along with 42 home runs and 101 RBIs. Another way the home run was eye-opening was the celebration at home plate, as he paid homage to Randy Arozarena , crossing his arms across his chest as he did during his 2020 postseason run to the World Series, with Caminero taking 38.7 seconds to boast.

articles.title: Brewers voice Jeff Levering on his pennant-clinching call and why he honored Bob Uecker
articles.summary: Twenty-three years ago, Jeff Levering was a designated hitter celebrating a Division III College World Series title at Chapman University, and nothing about...
articles.body:
Twenty-three years ago, Jeff Levering was a designated hitter celebrating a Division III College World Series title at Chapman University, and nothing about that night could have prepared him for where baseball would take him next. Now the longtime TV and radio voice of the Brewers has the best seat in the house as Milwaukee returns to the World Series for the first time since 1982, and he gave the pennant its soundtrack with his call of the final out of Game 4 against the Dodgers in the NLCS.

Awful Announcing recently caught up with him to find out what it has meant to narrate a season like this one.

Note: This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity.

Jeff Levering: "I got some sleep, but I did not go to the after-party, which I think was a pretty good decision on my part. After being on the air, the trophy ceremony, and the champagne and beer showers in the clubhouse, it was certainly a long night. There's no doubt it was a very fun one for everybody involved."

What was the atmosphere like when the team returned to Milwaukee?

"When we landed, we had the fire department out, and they gave us a water cannon (salute), which was amazing for the airplane. Fire trucks, police cars, and other emergency vehicles with their sirens on were waiting for us. I would say that fans were lined up for a good two miles from the airport until we got to the exit. They were at the ballpark waiting for the team to arrive and were cheering them on. So to say that the next week here in town is going to be crazy with Brewers fever would be an understatement."

Were you nervous at all as a broadcaster heading into Game 4?

"I went into the game treating it just like another game. As the game progressed, you can ramp yourself up for that situation. I always want to be the best I can be on any broadcast, whether it's a random Tuesday in June or a potential World Series clincher. I'm going to treat every game the same. Granted, the juices are going to flow a little differently in a potential clinch situation. But as soon as Garrett Mitchell hit the home run and the Brewers took the lead for the first time, that's when it started to kick in. Get yourself ready for the eighth and ninth innings because this could be it."

"I got the call back in the eighth inning; my partner, Lane Grindle, had the seventh. When he tossed him to me in the eighth, I remember looking up at the top of the radio booth at Dodger Stadium and taking a deep breath. Alright, here we go. For the last 12 outs, I was locked in, making sure I was on every pitch. There was no messing around. I wanted to make sure that if this was the night, I did the call (justice) for this fan base, I would do it. I think I accomplished that."

You got a lot of love for your final-out call in the NLCS. How did that call come about?

"I did not script anything. The only thing I wanted to get across was that the World Series was going to go through Wisconsin, and I thought that was important not just for the fans in Milwaukee but for the state of Wisconsin. They haven't experienced anything like this for 44 years. So, if they were in a situation to clinch and I was on the call for it, I wanted to make sure the fans in Wisconsin got their due credit. 'The Brewers win the pennant' thing. I didn't really think about that, to be honest. First and foremost, I want to get the play right. I wanted to make sure I called the play correctly first, then react in the moment, and that reaction was as authentic as you can get. That's what a lot of people gathered from the Harry Doyle character for Major League , and that's what came out. After I said the 'Brewers in the pennant,' my mind immediately went to 'Oh my god, the Brewers win the pennant,' even though that wasn't what he said in the movie."

Why do you think it was important to acknowledge Bob Uecker?

"Because he never had the opportunity to call his own championship series. He never got to call a World Series clincher. A lot of people don't remember that. He didn't call the clincher in 1982. He was doing TV and had responsibilities downstairs. Dwayne Mosley had the call on them beating the Angels and going to the World Series in 1982. The only clincher he ever called was in the movie Major League. He was on the mic for 54 years in the franchise's history, and I worked with him for ten of those. I had the opportunity to sit next to him. So I thought it was important for me to show how much I cared about him and how much his legacy means to this organization. By doing that in a subtle way through a couple of words, right off the cuff, I think it was appropriate in that moment."

What did you learn from working with Bob Uecker?

"First and foremost, and I mean this is more of a life thing than a broadcasting thing, you treat everybody the same way. And that's something that Bob was always so good at, and I've always tried to be that way. I try to treat everybody the same way and make people feel special. Then, on the broadcasting side, his biggest thing was: don't worry about what's going on on your phone or on a computer. The game will tell you everything you need to know, so look out there. That's where the stories are. You can always find something to talk about. So make sure you're paying attention to everything that's around you, and then tell the story and have fun. Heck, we're going to the ballpark. Might as well have a good time while we do it, and he's right."

People have preconceived notions about Red Sox, Yankees, Dodgers, and Cubs fans. What are Brewers fans like?

"This fan base is unlike any I've been around. This is the fourth organization I've worked for. You have passionate fan bases all over the country. But here's something about being in Milwaukee, with the tailgating and the gritty mentality of the people from this city and this state. They've been starving for this moment for so long. That's also something that went into the call at the end of the night for the fan base. They deserve this. They deserve the opportunity to have fun and play for a World Series championship. Almost half of their home dates sold out this year, and that's something they can really hang their hats on. It's been a really special season."

Is it fair to call this the highlight of your broadcasting career so far?

"I would agree with that. As a player, I won a College World Series, but that pales in comparison to having the opportunity to be in a clinching situation for the team you cover and seeing it advance to the World Series. There's nothing close to what this Brewers team did."

How many people have tried to reach you about World Series tickets?

"I've had a handful of people reach out. I have two tickets to each home game, and those are spoken for. But I've had a good number of requests, and even my parents, who live in California, are like, 'Hey, can we sit in the booth with you?' I went, 'Guys, it doesn't work that way. If this was June, maybe. But this is the World Series. We can't just give press passes to people to sit in the booth. It's not going to work that way. This isn't Rancho Cucamonga anymore.'"

articles.title: Palworld Fans Crown Their Favorite Pal in New Poll as Winter Update Is Teased
articles.summary: Sekhmet is Palworld's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-shaped Pal was voted the most popular by global players, scoring 49,637 votes.
articles.body:
Sekhmet is Palworld 's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-shaped Pal was voted the most popular by global players, scoring 49,637 votes. Solenne came in second with 37,425 votes, and Chillet was third with 34,625 votes. Spare a thought for little old Verdash, who, despite a green bouffant that would make any '90s emo kid proud, was at the bottom of the rankings with 1,479 votes.

Alongside the results, Pocketpair also teased a new update for this winter , Palworld: Side by Side. When I say "teased," I mean gave us three human silhouettes, sending the fandom into speculation mode about who the hidden characters could be. The prevailing Reddit theories are that the mystery figures are Auri, Zoe, and Saya, which would make sense, given that they were the top picks for most popular characters in the character rankings in the Pocketpair poll. All three are already in-game as faction leaders, or tower bosses, and given that Pocketpair made Zoe a recruitable companion after last year’s poll, it could mean that Side by Side will let players team up with the trio.

In an interview with Gaming World Interviews at Gamescom in August, Pocketpair head of publishing and communications John “Bucky” Buckley teased that Palworld’s next update would include something fans have been asking for. Pocketpair hasn’t confirmed whether that’s Side by Side. He also suggested the update’s timing was chosen to steer clear of November, presumably to avoid GTA 6’s release.

“It’s exciting for us at Pocketpair because we’re doing something that people have wanted for a long time,” he said. “We kind of considered it for 1.0, but it would have just pushed the release back too far. And, you know, not to be cliché, everyone’s saying it, but this year... something’s happening later [in the year]... So we didn’t want to go anywhere near the November kind of range.

“We’re doing something that’s really exciting, but it’s not big... We’re going to start the marketing on this soon. It’s not a huge thing. You don’t have to restart your game to experience it.”

If you're planning on heading back to the Palpagos Islands, take a look at all the new Pals added in Palworld 1.0 , plus a guide to all the Palworld bosses , and our interactive Palworld map .

articles.title: Fan Uses AI to Fix Oblivion Remastered PC Performance
articles.summary: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the modern era, but just like many other games running on Unreal 5, it was a technical mess. However, a fan has used Claude to create a performance mod that improves the game's performance.
articles.body:
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the modern era, but just like many other games running on Unreal 5, it was a technical mess. However, a fan has used Claude to create a performance mod that improves the game's performance.

When The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered came out back in April 2025, it was absolutely plagued with performance issues – something that's unfortunately become pretty normal these days. But, more than a year after launch, the performance issues are still there, with patch 1.2, the most recent on Steam, coming out all the way back in June 2025. And even after that patch, there were still significant performance problems.

It's little wonder, then, that the community would try to take matters into their own hands. Reddit user LTSharp posted on the ChatGPT subreddit , with a video showing the unpatched game running side-by-side with their patched version. And, while the raw increase to the frame rate isn't huge, LTSharp's patch greatly reduces the stutter, going from 66 hitches in the unpatched clip to just 11 in the patched version of the game.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered Screenshots

In their post, LTSharp says one of the reasons for the rocky frametimes was that "the game was reconstructing the whole lighting of a scene in each frame even when nothing was changing, which was obviously a huge strain on CPU that had to parse all this work on a single thread."

They then ran Claude Opus 5.5 alongside Oblivion Remastered and tasked it with identifying the problems, and after two weeks, ended up with a patch. Crucially, this mod wasn't created by just entering a quick prompt into Claude, hitting enter, and then calling it a day. LTSharp describes the process as "two weeks of intense work" with a lot of trial and error involved.

It seems like the biggest source of the improved performance is spreading the work to more CPU cores. At any given moment in LTSharp's video, CPU utilization jumps from 35-40% to 50-60% utilization, with around two extra threads (workers) engaged. And given that these samples were recorded on a rig with a 5800X, there's probably some more room for improvement there.

AI usage is one of the biggest controversies in gaming right now, but this seems to be a decent use of the technology. This was just a person who was disappointed that after "upgrading from 2070 Super to 9070 XT, the game continued to run poorly, with low fps and stuttering," and decided to use Claude to fix the problem, despite not having any background in software development. Luckily, they've posted their work on GitHub, and if someone who's relatively inexperienced was able to reduce stutters by this much, I imagine there may be developers who can create forks of this project that might be able to eliminate them altogether.

This project is in contrast to some of the most egregious uses of the technology recently, like Epic, which recently delayed a Star Wars shooter to implement an AI-first policy where 'no hand-written code' is allowed. Likewise, an Xbox Business Analyst recently went on Twitter and ranted about how the game industry is 'pretending' to not use AI, and even made bold claims like, "If you're a game developer refusing to believe that AI has a place in your future, you should not be in the business of being a business."

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not a Human Are Coming to Xbox | IDXBOX
articles.summary: Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on Xbox from publisher Critical Reflex.
articles.body:
Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on Xbox from publisher Critical Reflex.

As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, celebrated indie titles Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not a Human are making their way to Xbox for the very first time.

Physics-focused game Arctic Eggs tasks players with cooking eggs in — you guessed it — the Arctic. It sounds easy enough, but the game’s physics make this chore a true test of patience. And it’s not just eggs you’ll have to cook, either; you’ll pan fry anything from cockroaches to shot glasses, sausages, stingrays, and more, with the aim of feeding the city’s hungry inhabitants and possibly earning an audience with the Saint of Six Stomachs. Arctic Eggs, from developer The Water Museum, is available today (October 20, 2026) on Xbox Series X/S.

No, I’m Not a Human is an unsettling tale that follows a homeowner in an increasingly uninhabitable world. Players must decide who to shelter and who to turn away as the days grow hotter, with mysterious beings crawling out of the ground — beings that look, and sometimes behave, like humans. Pick the real people and wait out the apocalypse together; pick impostors and risk your housemates’ lives. No, I'm Not a Human will be available on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass in 2027.

Cult indie horror game Mouthwashing , first released in September 2024, is an exciting addition to the Xbox family. Set on a shipwrecked space freighter, players are responsible for managing its remaining crew as they slowly descend into madness and self-destruction. Mouthwashing is coming to Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass on October 29, 2026.

IGN gave Mouthwashing a glowing review, scoring it a sparkling 9 out of 10. Reviewer Ronny Barrier praised it as a "grimy, uncomfortable, and incredibly compelling, painting an unsettling picture of who we can be in our worst moments – and it doesn’t let us get away with it."

That’s not all; Critical Reflex will be sharing more information on its YouTube channel later today.

Critical Reflex is known for a bevy of strange and interesting games that often go viral on YouTube; they've published titles like Militsioner, where players must make their escape from a giant policeman who's watching their every move, and Buckshot Roulette , where, well... you play Russian Roulette with a shotgun, with a few additional mechanics mixed in.

articles.title: Fortnite's Nikki Skin Sparks Debate Among Horror Fans, With Some Calling for a Boycott
articles.summary: A vocal group of Fortnite players are calling for a boycott of Epic's battle royale game after a skin of Obsession’s Nikki Freeman, played by Inde Navarrette, sparked backlash among fans.
articles.body:
A vocal group of Fortnite players are calling for a boycott of Epic's battle royale game after a skin of Obsession’s Nikki Freeman, played by Inde Navarrette, sparked backlash among fans.

On October 20, Epic Games revealed that Nikki Freeman is coming to Fortnite in a special collaborative video with the character’s actress, Inde Navarrette. And while there’s no denying Obsession’s popularity — Nikki was one of the most-searched Halloween costumes on Google this year, after all — her inclusion as a purchasable skin in a video game is rubbing some fans the wrong way.

Warning: Major spoilers for Obsession below!

This uncomfortable reaction is in direct response to Nikki being the victim of Bear’s wish in Obsession . In the movie, Nikki’s body is overtaken by a malicious entity while the real Nikki is locked away in her own mind, unable to do anything but watch as the entity possessing her commits atrocities while wearing her skin.

Be careful what you wish for… Nikki is coming to Fortnite tomorrow 🪾 — Fortnite (@Fortnite) October 20, 2026

Be careful what you wish for… Nikki is coming to Fortnite tomorrow 🪾

She is also taken advantage of by Bear, who engages in intimacy with Nikki’s physical form without getting the consent of the real Nikki. (Bear becomes aware of this fact in the film, but decides against trying to save her, asking, ‘What’s so bad about being with me?’ to which Nikki replies, ‘I’ve never been with you, Bear.’)

Needless to say, making Nikki — who is a victim of rape — a playable character in a video game isn’t exactly being met with positivity from some folks in Fortnite’s playerbase. That’s not including her special emote, which sees her hold up Wiley E. Coyote-style signs reenacting the famous dinner scene where she flips out on Bear, or the skin’s recreation of her iconic frown.

“Wanting your rape victim character in a game as a fun element (ironically Nikki suffers from has no control on her body and mind in movie) is a f**king choice,” one user wrote on Twitter/X. “Also, f**k Fortnite too for this choice.”

“I kind of hate how Nikki was turned into a meme like this. It kinda overshadows the actual horrific s**t her character actually went through in the movie, in my opinion,” another said .

“So, lemme [make] this make sense: Fortnite is using a character who has a narrative about loss of coercion, loss of consent, psychological torment, and tragic violence for entertainment purposes? Fortnite monopolizing on obsession gives me the ick. I'm grossed out,” another argued .

A viral post , which has since been deleted, even called for a boycott of Fortnite altogether due to the skin — but another segment of the game's playerbase isn't on board with this idea, with several arguing that Nikki is merely a fictional character and that her Fortnite skin “isn’t that deep.”

“There’s obviously heated discussion surrounding Nikki being put into Fortnite, but I don't really get how the character [being] integrated into [the] game = not taking her story seriously. Most people BUY these things BECAUSE they care about a character, it's usually not for a punchline,” one said .

“Let’s please not try to reduce Nikki to just another ‘victim,’” another asked . “Yes, her story is horrific and tragic, but that does NOT mean we shouldn’t allow for her to appear in multi-media regardless of quality.”

“People have such a hard time comprehending that Nikki isn’t a real person and that she’s a fictional character,” yet another posed .

This isn’t the first time Nikki’s inclusion in other events an IPs has sparked a debate; she was also featured as a wandering character at Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights , which sparked its own discourse in the horror scene as to whether or not this was actually ethical (not to mention concerns about the actors’ safety). Indie Navarrette, for her part, seems to have no issue with the whole thing, even posing with one of the character's actors for a photo while visiting the theme park this October.

articles.title: Microsoft reportedly plans Xbox handheld in 2027, next-gen console in 2028
articles.summary: The next Xbox could cost between $1,200 and $1,800 if Microsoft doesn’t subsidize it.
articles.body: Microsoft is reportedly planning to launch an Xbox “next-generation handheld device” for the holiday season of 2027. The Xbox next-gen console, codename Project Helix, would then launch in the holidays of 2028, according to a new report from Fortune. The report doesn’t make it clear whether the handheld would be made by a manufacturer like Asus, or by Microsoft itself. Xbox teamed up with Asus for its Xbox Ally devices, which ran a modified version of Windows 11 with an Xbox mode enabled. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has also described Project Helix as a “family of devices,” suggesting that Microsoft’s next Xbox console may not be just one piece of hardware. Last year Microsoft and AMD announced a “strategic multi-year partnership” to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation console. It seems increasingly likely that this will include a range of “Xbox” devices, running on AMD’s new chips. The regular next-generation Xbox console may not arrive until 2028, though. Fortune reports that Microsoft is currently projecting that its Xbox Project Helix console may cost “between $1,200 to $1,800” for consumers, unless Microsoft is willing to subsidize the cost of the hardware. Microsoft’s Windows and Xbox teams have also reportedly clashed over what software will power the next-gen Xbox. That’s not terribly surprising given the two teams have clashed multiple times over the past 25 years of Xbox. It sounds like Xbox is now controlling the direction of the software on Helix, though. The report also touches on the rumored changes to Xbox Game Pass. Last month rumors emerged that Microsoft was working on an overhaul to Game Pass that will create tiers with or without ads, much like Netflix and other streaming services. Fortune says Xbox is looking at including add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer. This would make Game Pass a lot more flexible, but it’s not clear what happens to day one games and the overall price of Game Pass. One of Sharma’s first big moves as Xbox CEO was reversing the Game Pass price hikes, after she admitted internally that “Game Pass has become too expensive for players.” Xbox dropped future Call of Duty titles from day one on Game Pass, and brought prices back down for its subscription service. Fortune also reports that Sharma is planning a fresh round of Xbox layoffs this month, followed by more in November and January.

articles.title: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of layoffs
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is planning new rounds of layoffs for sometime this month, November, and January, according to Fortune. In July, Sharma announced a “reset” that included planned layoffs.
articles.body: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is planning new rounds of layoffs for sometime this month, November, and January, according to Fortune. In July, as part of an organizational “reset,” Sharma announced planned layoffs affecting 3,200 staffers over the course of Microsoft’s 2027 fiscal year, including 1,600 cuts at that time, and in September, Microsoft laid off around 260 employees. Sharma’s changes have also included letting Double Fine and Compulsion Games become independent again, though Senua developer Ninja Theory may close. The report also touches on speculation that Xbox may be spun off or sold, and Judson Althoff, the CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, seemed to downplay that idea to Fortune. “Asha is one of the best leaders we have at the whole company,” Althoff said to Fortune. “We would not have put her on a business we intend to sell. There’s going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell.” Sharma recently told The New York Times that “Xbox is not for sale.” Fortune’s report also said that Microsoft is planning to launch a “next-generation handheld device” in 2027 and its Project Helix console in 2028.

articles.title: Xbox's Next Console May Reportedly Cost As Much as $1,800, New Handheld Rumored to Launch Next Year Before Helix
articles.summary: A new report claims that Xbox expects its next-generation console to cost as much as $1,800 and is currently targeting a 2028 release.
articles.body:
A new report claims that Xbox expects its next-generation console to cost as much as $1,800 and is currently targeting a 2028 release.

A new article from Fortune claims that Microsoft has internally projected that its next Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix, will cost consumers between $1,200 - $1,800. The article notes that Microsoft could choose to subsidize those costs to come in at a lower price point, but unless the tech giant is will to take major losses on the console that would go beyond normal standards, it seems likely that the machine will still cost over $1,000.

Of course, maybe a miracle could happen and the costs for the parts could lower in the coming years, but the odds of that seem excessively low. It's not uncommon for platform holders to take a loss on hardware, as the real money is made on games and subscriptions. However, Xbox doesn't have the same market share that it had 15 years ago. It is harder to justify big gambles, but the cost of the hardware itself may be a gamble which puts Microsoft between a rock and a hard place.

Fortune noted that Microsoft has also moved up engineering deadlines on Project Helix, instructing the team to move faster on building the hardware. As a result, Microsoft has also employed the use of AI to improve the productivity. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told the outlet that they won't use “AI for AI’s sake,” and are using it to solve engineering and performance problems.

Fortune also revealed that Xbox is also planning to release a handheld by holiday 2027, though it's unclear how linked this will be to Project Helix. Sharma has stated before that Helix is a "family" of devices , so this handheld could be the first step. While some initially thought that may mean this generation will have another Xbox Series X and S situation, with one console that is more entry level and another that is for more hardcore players, it may be a bit different.

Instead of a weaker console, Xbox may leverage less power inside of a handheld, which may be more appealing and sensible. Xbox previously stated we would hear more about Project Helix by the end of year , so maybe we will learn more in November for the company's 25th anniversary.

Ultimately, it sounds like the next console generation is going to look a lot different than previous ones. PlayStation is also rumored to have its own handheld companion in the works and reports suggest that Sony will likely have a costly console as well. A recent rumor suggested that PS6's RAM and storage would cost $680 alone , which is already more than any PlayStation console's launch price except for the PS5 Pro. With the additional required components, it's expected the PS6 will also brush up against, if not exceed the $1,000 price point.

Ultimately, it seems like the age of the affordable console may be coming to an end, at least for now. Whether prices will ever come back down remains to be seen, but it doesn't seem like it will happen any time soon.

articles.title: The CyberPowerPC Gaming PC RTX 5060 Ti Prebuilt Gaming PC Drops to $1,249 at Walmart
articles.summary: Significantly more powerful than the Steam Machine.
articles.body:
Walmart is offering the best deal right now on an affordable 1080p-capable gaming PC. For a limited time, you can pick up a CyberPowerPC prebuilt gaming PC featuring the newest Intel Core Ultra 7 PLUS CPU and GeForce RTX 5060 Ti GPU for $1,249 with free shipping. It's much more powerful (and upgradeable) than the Steam Machine.

CyberPowerPC RTX 5060 Ti Gaming PC for $1,249

CyberPowerPC Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus RTX 5060 Ti 8GB Gaming PC (16GB/1TB)

The CyberPowerPC Gamer Supreme gaming PC is equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus CPU, GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and 1TB NVMe SSD. The Intel Core Ultra 7 270K is part of Intel's newest Arrow Lake Refresh desktop CPUs released earlier this year. It features 24 cores and a maximum turbo frequency of 5.5GHz and excels at both gaming and productivity tasks. It's cooled by a 360mm liquid AIO.

The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is the best 1080p GPU you'll find at this price

The RTX 5060 Ti graphics card is a great GPU for 1080p gaming. It outperforms the RTX 4060 Ti by about 20%, and the gap widens in games that support DLSS 4.5 . Note that this model has 8GB of VRAM, which means that although it will play most games at 1440p quite well, it will struggle with more demanding games that use a lot of VRAM. If you want to play games like Control: Resonant or The Blood of Dawnwalker at 1440p, then I'd suggest jumping to an RTX 5070 equipped gaming PC. There's actually one on sale for $1,449 , which isn't that much more.

This system is much more powerful than the Steam Machine

On a side note, this is a significantly more powerful computer than the $1,049 Steam Machine , which is equipped with a very low wattage CPU and a custom GPU equivalent to the Radeon RX 7600 or GeForce RTX 4060. Expect to see at the bare minimum a 30%-40% performance advantage favoring the RTX 5060 Ti gaming rig. The CyberPowerPC is also much easier to upgrade in the future, since it uses non-proprietary off-the-shelf parts and a classic midtower PC design.

articles.title: Police Confirm Nearly $1 Million Worth of Trading Cards Stolen in PSA FedEx Truck Heist
articles.summary: Police in Santa Ana, California estimate that more than $963,000 in collectible trading cards was stolen from a FedEx truck outside of PSA’s Santa Ana headquarters.
articles.body:
Police in Santa Ana, California estimate that more than $963,000 in collectible trading cards was stolen from a FedEx truck outside of PSA’s Santa Ana headquarters.

The theft went viral in mid-October after several card collectors reported that they had received emails from PSA (Professional Sports Authenticator) stating that a FedEx truck carrying their collections had been burglarized.

One of the most prominent voices in this conversation was a collector by the screen name SKY-B, who claimed that more than $100,000 worth of cards that he’d hand-delivered to PSA at a card show for grading were now lost in the ether.

I have an awful feeling PSA is going to be extremely unfair on what the values of these cards are. — SKY-B (@SKYBCards) October 17, 2026

"We will compensate you for the items from your order that were involved, which is based on fair market value up to the Maximum Insured Value ("MIV") you selected for each item." @natsturner, I pray you handle this and take care of everyone affected in the most professional manner possible. I have an awful feeling PSA is going to be extremely unfair on what the values of these cards are.

PSA responded to the situation in a statement to IGN , outlining their plans to refund the affected customers and cooperate with both FedEx and law enforcement to investigate the burglary.

A day later, Santa Ana police have released a statement about the theft, as well as the eyewatering dollar amount that was stolen — and it’s far more than was originally calculated.

The theft occurred on October 13 outside of PSA’s headquarters in Santa Ana, California when a FedEx driver reportedly left their truck parked nearby for around 60 to 90 minutes. The thieves were able to break the truck’s lock and make off with the packages stored inside during this time.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign Cards

According to police, two pallets holding an estimated 100 packages were stolen, as well as a third pallet carrying around 50 packages. Law enforcement officials estimate that the total dollar amount of the first two pallets adds up to around $963,000. No dollar amount has yet been calculated for the third pallet, but given what we already know, it’s looking likely that the total damage will ring up to more than $1 million.

“The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokémon cards,” the SAPD told The Athletic . “The exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined, pending further investigation. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the Santa Ana Police Department.”

FedEx also released a statement, saying “the security of our customers’ shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation.”

PSA, for its part, has promised to refund customers “based on fair market value up to the Maximum Insured Value" of their cards and has deactivated the certificates of the stolen items.

"We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset. Our team is focused on supporting them. We take this incident seriously, and we will continue working with law enforcement to hold those responsible accountable,” it said.
